videos.summary: Skratch tests whether the new Aura hero Holfast can replace a maxed Inspiration 5 Lincos. Testing in Temporal Vortex shows that swapping Lincos for Holfast increased total Aura team damage from approximately 7.2B to 8.1B (and overall team damage by roughly 1B). Because Holfast's 20-second 30% Damage Up buff from his passive does not stack with Lincos's ultimate 30% Damage Up, running both together is redundant and Lincos becomes obsolete. Diantha remains essential in the lineup for Defense Down and utility, while Holfast serves as the primary offensive buffer and personal damage dealer.

heroes.note: Provides consistent 30% Damage Up via his passive/talent, channels Aura energy, and provides substantial personal damage along with random offensive buffs.

heroes.note: His 30% Damage Up does not stack with Holfast's passive, rendering even an Inspiration 5 copy obsolete in top-tier Aura comps.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.note: Carries team damage output completely in fast dungeon runs and Temporal Vortex regardless of secondary support choices.

heroes.name: Diantha
heroes.note: Should not be removed for Holfast because she provides Defense Down and essential utility.

heroes.name: Solmo
heroes.note: Used as the frontline support for shields and team survivability in Temporal Vortex.

teams.note: Aura team setup that outdamaged the Lincos variation by almost 1 billion damage, dealing over 8B Aura damage.

Equip Holfast with full mythical DPS gear or Puppeteer set to maximize his personal damage contributions.

videos.summary: Gorax provides a comprehensive guide for maximizing damage against the endgame boss Undyne Inferno - Cypreum (Resurgent Dragon). He showcases multiple high-end and budget team compositions across Toxin, Radiant/Aura, Dauntless, Necrosis/Shadow, and Frost schools, with many surpassing 200M to over 3B damage. The guide explains boss mechanics, specifically how to manage the boss's Power of Dragon Rage stacks using ultimate energy manipulation. Detailed 20-second skill timing rotations and gearing priorities are broken down to ensure maximum damage uptime and survivability.

heroes.note: Reaches up to 3B damage against Cypreum when built with high Enlightenment, Attack, and Accuracy.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.note: Performs on par with Serpentemis at high inspiration; built with Crit Rate, Crit Damage, and high HP.

heroes.name: Child of Chaos
heroes.note: Mitigates the boss's Attack Penalty debuff and can solo sustain team survivability even at low inspiration.

heroes.name: Oggok
heroes.note: Provides healing and immortality; his 'Born to Be Proud' talent gives energy on ally resist to enable 18-second rotations.

heroes.name: Sleight
heroes.note: Essential derivative damage dealer; built offensively with Enlightenment, Accuracy, and Attack.

heroes.name: Sacredeia
heroes.note: Provides a crucial 30% Poison Vulnerability debuff with Mystic Conch, significantly raising team damage.

heroes.name: Durango
heroes.note: Can replace Sacredeia for applying Corrosion/Toxin, though overall team output drops due to lacking her 30% vulnerability debuff.

heroes.name: Shahla
heroes.note: Grants ultimate energy to allies, which actively removes the boss's Power of Dragon Rage stacks.

heroes.name: Anneliesis
heroes.note: Positioned behind Talethia to boost and protect her while providing debuffs and sustain.

heroes.name: Holfast
heroes.note: Scales massively with higher inspirations; built purely for offensive Radiant damage.

heroes.name: Maashtur
heroes.note: Reduces enemy ultimate energy on his skill, effectively stripping Dragon Rage stacks from the boss.

heroes.name: Nathaniel
heroes.note: Replaces offensive supports when survival is an issue, providing debuff cleansing, shields, and Resistance sharing.

heroes.name: Saverio
heroes.note: Main damage dealer for Shadow/Necrosis comps; easily deals 370M+ damage built with Enlightenment and Attack.

heroes.name: Usha
heroes.note: Anchor for an all-epic/rare Frost team that reliably clears over 200M damage.

teams.note: High-end Toxin team doing nearly 3B damage on a 20s skill rotation with Child of Chaos handling buffs and survival.
Budget Toxin setup using epics and rares capable of easily surpassing 200M damage with Enlightenment builds.
Premier Aura/Radiant composition hitting over 2B damage; Shahla provides ultimate energy to strip dragon rage stacks.
High-damage Dauntless composition doing 500M–600M damage; Maashtur controls boss ultimate energy.
Defensive Dauntless variant using Nathaniel for debuff dispels and shields, hitting 610M damage.
Necrosis/Shadow comp achieving 370M+ damage running purely default skill timings.
Budget Frost composition of epics/rares that reaches 239M+ damage without legendary inspirations.

meta_changes: Resurgent Dragon (Undyne Inferno - Cypreum) introduces the 'Power of Dragon Rage' passive, granting 8 stacks that must be reduced by increasing ally ultimate energy or decreasing boss ultimate energy.
Puppeteer artifact sets trigger boss mechanics that consume stacks while nullifying the set's stat benefits, shifting rotation strategies away from strict 18-second loops to 20-second loops.
tips: Run a 20-second rotation on your skills rather than an 18-second rotation to prevent boss mechanics from desyncing Puppeteer sets and ultimate sequences.
Counter the boss's Dragon Rage stacks by using heroes that grant ally ultimate energy (like Shahla) or reduce enemy ultimate energy (like Maashtur).
In Phase 1 of the dragon, prioritize Enlightenment, Attack, and Accuracy over Resistance; save heavy Resistance gear for Phase 2.
If your team struggles to survive under Child of Chaos alone, swap a secondary damage dealer for Oggok built with high Resistance and the 'Born to Be Proud' talent.

videos.summary: This guide covers the best priorities when forging Mythic gear through the Piece of Treasury feature. Players should prioritize crafting Armor and Gloves first because they can roll multiple primary attributes. For sets, Strike the Unprepared (+30% damage under Defense Penalty) is universally best for main DPS, followed by Dragonflame Scorch for single-target bosses or Arcane Eye's Requiem for AoE teams. Crit-based teams should aim for Crit Damage gloves and ATK% armor with Crit Rate substats, while Enlightenment teams should prioritize ATK% gloves with Enlightenment and Enlightenment armor with ATK%.
tips: Forge Armor and Gloves first when using Piece of Treasury because they have multiple primary attribute options.

Forge Dragonflame Scorch for up to +24% bonus damage on single-target boss encounters.
Forge Arcane Eye's Requiem for up to +20% damage on AoE teams (Toxin, Burn, Corrosion).
For Crit damage teams (Ice Blast, Dauntless, Corrosion), craft Gloves with Crit Damage main stat and Armor with ATK% main stat, tuning substats to reach 100% Crit Rate.
For Enlightenment teams (Wild, Toxin, Shadow), craft Gloves with ATK% main stat and enhanced Enlightenment substats, and Armor with Enlightenment main stat and enhanced ATK% substats.

videos.summary: This video previews high-end Continental Challenge team compositions used on the Chinese server for Season 9. The creator breaks down optimal setups for Dauntless, Aura, Ice Blast, and Corrosion teams against various bosses. Key builds focus heavily on specific rotation timings (15-second vs. 18-second rotations) and high effect resistance to resist boss debuffs. A new mythic chest piece that stacks damage-amplifying debuffs is featured across multiple damage dealers.

heroes.name: Guinavivre
heroes.note: Needs 100% crit rate, followed by maximum attack and attack speed runes to maximize shield and damage scaling.

heroes.name: Nastjenka
heroes.note: Built with 75%+ crit rate and massive crit damage, requiring less attack speed than Guinavivre.

heroes.name: Kurvida
heroes.note: Built with high skill haste for a 15-second rotation, high accuracy, and attack to share via mythic gear.

heroes.name: Maashtur
heroes.note: Equipped with Antler's artifact and high accuracy to shield and boost the highest-attack ally.

heroes.name: Selva
heroes.note: Uses the Puppeteer set, high accuracy, and resistance to delay and extend debuffs on bosses.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.note: Scales heavily off HP, crit rate, and crit damage, benefiting greatly when paired with max-HP buffers.

heroes.name: Holfast
heroes.note: Directly replaces Lincos even at Inspiration 0 and can deal substantial supplementary damage.

heroes.name: Rena
heroes.note: Provides team-wide haste enabling a 15-second skill rotation that outdamages Celestine and Sagomir variants.

heroes.name: Celestine
heroes.verdict: Alternative Aura support / Ice Blast enabler
heroes.note: Extends team HP to bolster Talethia's damage output, but is also used in Ice Blast setups.

heroes.name: Beldelle
heroes.note: Requires full crit rate and pure attack with her exclusive artifact, completely skipping crit damage.

heroes.name: Shinnah
heroes.note: Built with 300+ resistance and 240+ accuracy to prevent team debuffs and shred enemy defenses.

heroes.name: Fredegonda
heroes.note: Built with maximum crit rate, crit damage, and over 250 resistance to stay debuff-free against Stegamoffyn.

heroes.name: Rook
heroes.note: Prioritizes 100% crit rate, max crit damage, and skill haste over raw attack stats.

heroes.name: Szecedith
heroes.note: Equipped with her exclusive artifact, built with high attack, crit rate, and crit damage to maintain corrosion stacks.

heroes.name: Child of Chaos
heroes.note: Built with maximum HP, Puppeteer set, accuracy, and skill haste to enable a 15-second team rotation.

heroes.name: Reytah
heroes.note: Remains viable at Inspiration 0, building HP, accuracy, and skill haste to extend corrosion debuffs.

teams.note: High-investment Dauntless team tuned around 18s (or 15s with haste) skill timings, utilizing Selva to extend debuffs.
Aura team hitting 2.58B damage; uses Rena for a fast 15-second rotation. Celestine or Sagomir can substitute Rena.
Ice Blast team dealing ~1.6B damage with 18-second skill timings and heavy team-wide resistance (250-300+).
Corrosion team dealing ~1B damage through AoE corrosion stacking, running Rook on default skill timings.

meta_changes: A new mythic chest armor piece is introduced that stacks damage-amplifying debuffs on the boss.
Holfast replaces Lincos in Aura teams as the premier support even at Inspiration 0.
15-second rotation cycles enabled by Rena's haste significantly outperform standard 18-second rotations in Aura compositions.
tips: For Guinavivre and Rook, guarantee 100% crit rate before focusing on secondary stats.
Beldelle in Ice Blast should skip crit damage completely and stack pure crit rate and attack.
Aim for 250-300+ effect resistance on supports when fighting bosses like Stegamoffyn to prevent deadly debuff loops.
Build Child of Chaos with accuracy and skill haste runes so your Corrosion team can sync on 15-second rotations.

videos.summary: This guide covers team compositions, gear setups, skill timings, and export codes for Week 3 of the Continental Challenge (Imperial Shadow Recast), requiring six separate teams. Detailed breakdowns are provided for Tamar using Poison/Toxin, Khrysos using Dauntless, Vinyara using Necrosis/Shadow, Twitch using Aura, and Vasska using Frost/Necrosis. The video highlights both premium high-investment rosters capable of hundreds of millions in damage and accessible free-to-play alternatives utilizing epic and rare units to easily achieve the 12 million S-rank damage threshold. Specific encounter mechanics, such as positioning Lothair behind Tamar and utilizing Fitz's debuff transfers against Vasska, are explained.

heroes.name: Lothair
heroes.note: Needs Enlightenment and Attack; jumping behind Tamar at 40 poison stacks prevents attack penalties.

heroes.name: Serpentemis
heroes.verdict: Core damage dealer for Poison teams
heroes.note: Built with high Enlightenment, Attack, and Accuracy; stays safely in position and resists stuns due to self-buffs.

heroes.name: Child of Chaos
heroes.note: Switched to Poison element with Dragonbone Catalyst and Puppeteer set to boost team damage.

heroes.name: Sleight
heroes.note: Requires over 250 Resistance to survive Tamar's targeted damage while stacking Accuracy and offensive stats.

heroes.name: Sacredeia
heroes.note: Carries Misty Conch artifact to apply Defense Penalty and benefits from defensive stats and Resistance.

heroes.name: Guinavivre
heroes.note: Built for Crit Rate, Crit Damage, Attack, Attack Speed, and Resistance to avoid Khrysos's attack speed debuffs.

heroes.name: Fathomdown
heroes.note: Can enable versatile F2P teams to deal over 100M damage when built with high Skill Haste, Hourglass, and Resistance.

heroes.name: Deverick
heroes.note: Applies Attack Penalty and dispels Vinyara's defensive buffs to neutralize her 30% damage reduction and 60% Defense Up.

heroes.name: Saverio
heroes.note: Built with high Enlightenment and Attack to leverage Shadow energy resets for rapid damage bursts.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.note: Scales directly with HP percentage stats across off-pieces and runes along with standard Crit stats.

heroes.name: Solmo
heroes.note: Provides team-wide shields, healing, and Resistance sharing against Twitch's heavy debuffs.

heroes.name: Fitz
heroes.verdict: Key rare tech hero for Vasska
heroes.note: Transfers attack penalties from the entire team back onto himself with his ultimate, enabling Frost allies to deal full damage.

heroes.name: Voresh
heroes.note: Applies Buff Prohibition via Puppeteer set and Witch's Remains to lower the boss's damage output.

heroes.name: Torrin
heroes.note: Grants Invisibility and groups enemies together; requires enough Skill Haste to align his ultimate within an 18-second rotation.

teams.note: Full Poison team running an 18-second rotation; capable of 800M–1.8B damage depending on Inspiration levels.
High-end Dauntless composition built with Resistance on an 18-second rotation dealing 200M–500M damage.
Versatile Dauntless variant utilizing Fathomdown with high Skill Haste to easily deal 70M–100M+ damage.
Shadow/Necrosis composition running on default timing, hitting over 200M damage with Deverick handling boss buffs.
HP-scaling Aura team on an 18-second cycle dealing 500M–700M damage with Solmo providing sustain.
Frost/Necrosis team dealing 240M damage using Fitz's debuff redirection and Torrin's grouping on an 18-second cycle.

tips: Against Tamar, manually time Lothair to leap behind the boss right at 40 poison stacks so he permanently avoids Tamar's attack penalties.
For boss encounters with heavy debuffs like Khrysos and Tamar, build key units with 200+ Resistance or utilize the 'Stand United' talent to share Resistance.
Against Vinyara, ensure you bring a buff dispeller like Deverick to strip her 30% damage reduction and 60% defense buffs.
Against Vasska, rare hero Fitz can redirect all attack penalties from allies to himself, allowing rare and epic Frost units to deal massive damage.
Standardize team ultimate cooldowns around an 18-second skill rotation cycle to align with Continental Challenge boss ability windows.

He breaks down ideal gear combinations for both raw damage dealers (like Talethia) and Enlightenment derivative DPS (like Serpentemis). heroes.name: Guinavivre

Team 2 utilizes a Toxin composition with Child of Chaos acting as the solo support alongside Twitch, Sleight, Sacredeia, and Serpentemis on an 18-second rotation. Sacredeia wears a Puppeteer set acquired early via Walker's Trail or Fey Meander.

heroes.name: Maashtur
heroes.note: Needs to be built with the highest HP on the Dauntless team to soak hits.

heroes.name: Guinavivre
heroes.note: Equipped with her exclusive artifact and built prioritizing Critical Rate and damage.

heroes.name: Child of Chaos
heroes.note: Built with Rift Hourglass for Skill Haste and sufficient Accuracy to guarantee debuffs without needing an exclusive artifact.

heroes.name: Sacredeia
heroes.note: Utilized as the carrier for the 3-piece Puppeteer set to enable an 18-second team rotation.

heroes.name: Serpentemis
heroes.note: Built stacking high Enlightenment (over 350) and Accuracy for maximum damage.

videos.summary: This guide covers four optimized teams and variations for Week 2 of Continental Challenge against Vasska, Twitch, Khrysos, and Tamar. For Vasska, a Frost/Necrosis team utilizes Fitz's ultimate to absorb undispellable Attack penalties alongside Voresh's Buff Prohibition. The Twitch encounter is tackled using a high-Resistance Radiance Aura team that capitalizes on stage damage buffs triggered by resisting debuffs. Against Khrysos, a Lightning Dauntless team stacks Attack Speed and Resistance, while Tamar is countered with a high-damage Toxin team using a manual targeting trick on Lothair.

heroes.name: Fitz
heroes.verdict: Core tank and debuff cleanser for Vasska
heroes.note: Transfers the boss's undispellable Attack penalties from allies to himself using his ultimate.

heroes.name: Voresh
heroes.note: Applies Buff Prohibition to prevent Vasska's Attack and Attack Speed buffs while providing healing and Defense Penalty.

heroes.name: Torrin
heroes.note: Built with high Skill Haste to cycle Puppeteer set buffs on an 18-second rotation while sharing defensive stats with Fitz.

heroes.name: Vidimir
heroes.note: Deals massive damage without needing Accuracy when geared with 100% Critical Rate and high Critical Damage.

heroes.name: Solmo
heroes.note: Built with over 500 Resistance and Titan Rib to provide team-wide shields and damage buffs upon resisting debuffs.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.verdict: Top Radiance Aura DPS for Twitch
heroes.note: Scales heavily with Max HP% and Critical stats to deliver the bulk of the Aura team's AoE damage.

heroes.name: Maashtur
heroes.note: Reduces boss Attack and Recharge Speed while providing massive shields and taking damage for allies.

heroes.name: Nathaniel
heroes.note: Epic Lightning support that dispels debuffs, provides shielding with Aurelium Vest, and shares Resistance through talents.

heroes.name: Child of Chaos
heroes.verdict: Core cleanser and buffer for Tamar
heroes.note: Uses the Puppeteer set and high Attack to reliably cleanse crowd control and debuffs from the team.

heroes.name: Lothair
heroes.note: Deals immense damage when geared with Enlightenment and Resistance, especially when manually positioned to avoid boss debuffs.

heroes.name: Serpentemis
heroes.note: Achieves massive scaling with high Enlightenment, Attack, and at least 150 Accuracy.

teams.note: Budget-friendly Frost/Necrosis setup capable of over 200M damage; Fitz absorbs Attack penalties while Voresh prevents boss self-buffs.
Radiance Aura composition stacking high Resistance to quickly cap the stage's 200-stack Attack buff and trigger Titan Rib.
Lightning Dauntless team tuned with Resistance runes to negate Attack Speed debuffs; Nathaniel can replace Maashtur if needed.
High-scoring Toxin team reaching over 1B damage; manually time Lothair's first ultimate to keep him out of Tamar's debuff cone.

tips: Align all skill timings to an 18-second recast interval when triggering the Puppeteer armor set bonus.
Against Twitch and Tamar, build high Resistance (ideally 300+) on your heroes to prevent crippling Attack penalties and trigger bonus stage buffs.
On Tamar, manually trigger Lothair's first ultimate after reaching 40 Poison stacks and aim it away from the center to prevent him from being targeted by Tamar's Attack Penalty II.
Tune Fitz's ultimate cast to 23 seconds on Vasska so he cleanses and redirects the boss's undispellable Attack penalty right before your DPS heroes burst.

Longbeau provides unmatched utility by dispelling and reflecting debuffs via Black Rat while inflicting Buff Prohibition and Healing Restriction. Fyrenzur introduces allied Dodge mechanics and counter-attacks, though her heavy RNG reliance makes her more suited for PvP or Magi-Chess than reliable PvE. Tallyn offers exceptional crowd control and survivability as a Lightning tank, making him a great disrupter against backline threats in PvP and Fey Meander.

heroes.name: Longbeau
heroes.verdict: Best overall pick of the three supports
heroes.note: Counters debuff-heavy enemies like Serpentemis by reflecting negative effects, inflicting 100% Buff Prohibition, and giving massive damage resistance shields.

heroes.name: Fyrenzur
heroes.note: Provides team-wide Dodge buffs and retaliatory healing/damage upon dodging, but high RNG makes her inconsistent for PvE boss encounters.

heroes.name: Tallyn
heroes.verdict: Strong crowd control tank for PvP and Fey Meander
heroes.note: Charges furthest backline threats to apply Knock Up and Attack Penalty, while dishing out constant stuns, Resistance Penalty, and ultimate energy reduction.

teams.note: Tallyn tanks and provides AoE Resistance Penalty and stuns to set up high damage from Thunderbolt carries.

meta_changes: S9 Targeted Summons banner allows selecting a targeted new legendary support at 300 summons, with a guaranteed exclusive support at 1,000 summons.
Introduction of true debuff reflection mechanics via Longbeau's Black Rat, bypassing enemy resistance.
Introduction of team-wide Dodge mechanics and dodge-triggered counters via Fyrenzur.
tips: Save 300 Heliolite Dice for the start of Season 9 to secure a selectable legendary support from the Targeted Summons banner.
Pick Longbeau if you prioritize guaranteed reliability in PvE and anti-debuff utility in PvP over RNG dodge mechanics.
Consider equipping Mystic Horn on Fyrenzur to maximize value from her frequent Attack Penalty applications.

videos.summary: Syonis is a new Necrosis element DPS hero from the Shadow school debuting in Season 9 as the first DPS banner hero. His kit revolves around granting Attack Up to Shadow allies, shredding enemy Defense based on Enlightenment, and isolating the enemy's highest Attack unit into a 1v1 Energy Drain Zone. He is tailored specifically for PvP and Magic Chess, capable of shutting down dangerous burst carries like Serpentemis, bypassing immortality buffs at Inspiration 2. However, because Shadow teams remain lackluster in PvE content, he is generally considered a lower-priority pull for players seeking broad PvE progression.

heroes.name: Syonis
heroes.note: Dominates PvP by locking down the highest Attack enemy in a 1v1 zone and bypassing immortality, but is the least worthy pick if looking to build PvE teams.

heroes.name: Saverio
heroes.note: Combines with Syonis to quickly wipe enemy squads in early PvP rotations thanks to fast initial Shadow Energy gains.

heroes.name: Serpentemis
heroes.note: A top-tier PvP threat whose AoE burst can be neutralized by Syonis pulling her into his Energy Drain Zone.

teams.note: Fast Shadow burst composition designed to rapidly generate Shadow Energy and demolish enemy teams within the first two rotations.

meta_changes: Syonis introduces the Energy Drain Zone mechanic, isolating the highest Attack enemy and himself into a 1v1 duel where outside units cannot target them, energy regeneration is locked, and immortality can be bypassed at Inspiration 2.

His passive aura reduces enemy Defense based on Enlightenment (up to 50%, or 60% with Inspiration 5), but prevents affected targets from receiving other Defense Reduction debuffs like Witch's Remains.
tips: Build Enlightenment on Syonis to maximize the passive Defense Reduction aura in front of him.
Target Inspiration 2 if building him for high-end PvP, as it cleanses crowd control upon casting his Ultimate and allows his damage to completely ignore immortality effects.
Avoid prioritizing Syonis if your primary goal is PvE progression, as Shadow school teams remain weak in PvE environments compared to other schools.

heroes.note: Absorbs damage into permanent ally stat buffs, cleanses, applies Karmic Sin, and reaches peak efficiency at Inspiration 2.

heroes.name: Sia

Holfast and Rhyviel heavily boost the viability of dedicated Aura and Corrosion archetype team compositions.

Target Inspiration 2 on Celestine for a permanent 15% team damage reduction and 15% damage bonus.
Build Syonis with very high Enlightenment to cap out his passive defense reduction aura at 50% (or 60% at Inspiration 5).

videos.summary: This video provides an early kit showcase and test server analysis of Rhyviel, a new Legendary Poison/Corrosion damage dealer introduced in Season 9. Rhyviel applies Rending Bite, which shreds enemy Defense by up to 35%, reduces incoming damage, amplifies Corrosion accumulation, and applies 30% Poison Vulnerability via talents. In a low-level Temporal Vortex test against Arbor Hydra Diana, Rhyviel demonstrated strong secondary DPS capabilities behind Rook while providing massive team utility. Gorax breaks down Rhyviel's skills, inspirations, recommended gear stats, and his role in late-game Corrosion compositions.

heroes.name: Rhyviel
heroes.verdict: High-tier secondary DPS and essential Corrosion amplifier
heroes.note: Applies 35% Defense reduction and 30% Poison Vulnerability via Rending Bite, amplifies Corrosion accumulation, and deals high True Damage based on active Corrosion.

heroes.name: Rook
heroes.note: Remains the highest damage dealer in Corrosion setups by consuming Corrosion stacks to deal massive True Damage.

heroes.name: Szecedith
heroes.note: Acts as a reliable Corrosion applier to fuel Rhyviel and Rook's True Damage scaling.

heroes.name: Sacredeia
heroes.note: Provides Poison Vulnerability and Corrosion application, synergizing well with the Misty Conch artifact.

teams.note: Corrosion boss team where Szecedith and Sacredeia ramp up Corrosion stacks, Rhyviel shreds Defense and inflicts Poison Vulnerability, and Rook deals massive True Damage.

meta_changes: Rhyviel introduces guaranteed high Defense shred (35%) and Poison Vulnerability into Corrosion teams, significantly elevating overall Corrosion archetype viability.
tips: Build Rhyviel with standard offensive stats: Attack, Crit Rate, and Crit Damage; his exclusive artifact Swamp Toadstool is an excellent choice.
Target Inspiration 2 on Rhyviel if possible, as it raises Rending Bite application to 100% chance (removing RNG) and gives a 5% team damage boost against afflicted targets.

Multiple teams, including Toxin and Necrosis/Shadow, performed effectively on full auto without precise manual timing.

heroes.name: Zeffi
heroes.note: Brings Defense Up, invincibility, and buff dispelling to strip Mekkatorque's Defense Up.

heroes.name: Shahla
heroes.note: Built with high Resistance and Prismatic Cloak to reflect attack penalties and cycle ultimate energy into the team on a 15-second rotation.

heroes.name: Feenja
heroes.note: Provides Resistance Up II, shields, and bonus Resistance sharing via Stand United to stop Mekkatorque from draining ultimate energy.

heroes.name: Rook
heroes.note: Needs high Resistance gear to avoid having his ultimate energy drained by the boss.

heroes.name: Calavera
heroes.note: Replaced Durango alongside Serpentemis and Twitch, helping the Toxin team reach 900M damage.

heroes.note: Built with Misty Conch and elevated Resistance to ensure clean 15-second skill cycling against Mekkatorque.

heroes.name: Astaion
heroes.note: Rebuilt with high HP, Resistance, and accuracy on Witch's Remains to survive boss burst and sustain the Shadow team.

meta_changes: Phase 2 of Mekkatorque introduces heavy ultimate energy drain and recharge penalties alongside increased boss attack power, making Resistance and Resistance Up buffs mandatory to maintain damage rotations.
tips: Prioritize Resistance on your main DPS heroes (like Rook and Twitch) or bring Resistance Up buffers like Feenja so Mekkatorque cannot deplete their ultimate charge.
Equip Shahla with Prismatic Cloak to reflect the boss's attack penalties back onto him.
Equip Feenja with Gatekeeper's Staff and Secrecy Order's Chant to boost allied attack through shielding.
Do not overcomplicate skill timings; running teams like Toxin and Shadow on full auto can produce equal or higher damage than rigid timing presets.

heroes.name: Anneliesis
heroes.note: Requires 60+ Skill Haste to ensure ultimate aligns with the 15-second team rotation; built with Titan Rib artifact, Secrecy Order set, and Wildsand Devotion.

heroes.note: Shares Attack to Talethia via Everlasting Candleflame set; built with Resistance, Puppeteer set, and Angelic Alliance without needing Skill Haste.

heroes.name: Diantha
heroes.note: Equipped with Punisher's Whip and Conflagration of Bones (Bleed debuff); targets 320+ to 356 Accuracy and Resistance.

heroes.name: Lincos
heroes.note: Needs 72+ Skill Haste to sustain the 15-second rotation, which may require running two 2-piece Skill Haste sets (Astrologer and Secrecy Order) if rune substats fall short.

teams.note: Deals 1.68B to 1.75B+ damage using a 15-second rotation (Talethia recasts at 13.8s, Pet at 30s) alongside the Golden Tressym pet.

tips: Ensure Talethia has the highest Attack on the team so Shahla shares her Attack buff directly to her.
Hit at least 60 Skill Haste on Anneliesis and 72 Skill Haste on Lincos to maintain proper ultimate sync on a 15-second recast cycle.
If rune rolls lack enough Skill Haste substats, combine 2-piece Secrecy Order with 2-piece Astrologer to gain an extra +40 Skill Haste from set bonuses.
Aim for 320+ (ideally up to 356) Accuracy and Resistance on Diantha to reliably land debuffs and withstand boss mechanics.

videos.summary: This guide breaks down three top-performing team archetypes for Temporal Vortex (stages I through IV): Toxin, Aura, and Dauntless. The boss operates on a strict 20-second skill rotation featuring a massive single-target nuke aimed at the ally with the highest HP, making HP stat manipulation on tanks crucial. Teams utilizing a 3-piece Puppeteer set synchronize their DPS ultimates to an 18-second cycle, timed precisely around debuffs and buffs. Toxin provides massive derivative damage when built around Serpentemis and Lothair/Sleight, while Aura relies on Talethia scaling with max HP, and Dauntless functions as an ultra-high ceiling single-target whale setup led by Guinavivre and Maashtur.

heroes.note: Primary damage dealer for Toxin teams who scales massively off Enlightenment and Attack with Fearless Challenge and Precise Carnage gear.

heroes.name: Lothair
heroes.note: Excels as a secondary damage dealer whose damage scales on active Toxin stacks; works best with his exclusive artifact Nightfall Pallium.

heroes.note: Provides vital Toxin and Potent Medicine application; equipped with Three-Ears Emblem to amplify team elemental damage.

heroes.name: Oggok

heroes.name: Child of Chaos
heroes.note: Provides team-wide buffs, debuffs, and cleanses, while his Death's Portent deals massive bonus damage scaling entirely off his Attack stat.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.note: Deals massive damage scaling on max HP, requiring an HP% chest and negative rune while keeping the highest Attack in the Aura team to receive Lincos's buff.

heroes.name: Lincos
heroes.note: Provides a crucial 30% damage boost for 10s to the Aura ally with highest Attack and wears Puppeteer to enable the 18-second rotation.

heroes.note: Secondary damage dealer built with 230+ Accuracy and Witch's Remains to reliably inflict Defense Penalty II.

heroes.note: Must be geared with highest team HP and Aurelium Vest to tank the single-target boss hit while providing ramping shield value.

heroes.note: Increases Critical Damage for the highest Attack Aura ally, though replaceable by Child of Chaos or Anneliesis.

heroes.name: Maashtur
heroes.note: Absorbs the boss's nuke with maximum HP while applying crucial Attack Penalty and team buffs.

heroes.name: Guinavivre

videos.summary: The creator reviews the upcoming Server Transfer pre-registration feature and criticizes its heavy limitations. Transferring requires a new item called Realm Compass, which costs Dragon Crystals (2,000 for the first transfer, 5,000 for the second, and 10,000 for the third), completely excluding free-to-play players. To transfer, players must receive invitations from three players ranked in the top 30 of the target server's Time Sand leaderboard, and each target server is strictly capped at receiving only three travelers. Transfers must be initiated before Season Day 62 on servers that have completed at least three seasons, followed by a 180-day cooldown. The creator argues this feature fails to revive low-population servers and urges developers to implement server merges instead.
meta_changes: Introduction of the Server Transfer Pre-registration feature using the new Realm Compass item.
Servers that have completed at least three seasons can receive incoming transfers, capped at a maximum of three travelers per server.
Transfers require approvals from three target-server players who are ranked in the top 30 of Time Sand rankings.
Server transfers incur a 180-day account cooldown upon completion.
tips: Transfer reservations must be submitted before Season Day 62; transfers cannot be initiated past this cutoff.
Ensure you have contact with top 30 ranked players on your intended target server before applying, as you need three invites within 48 hours.

Budget Dragon Crystals if you plan to transfer: the Realm Compass costs 2,000 Dragon Crystals for the first transfer, 5,000 for the second, and 10,000 for the third, and cannot be bought with Wyrmarrow.
Consider the 180-day transfer cooldown carefully before locking yourself into a new server.

videos.summary: Skratch visited the Dragonheir development studio to interview the developers about community concerns and future updates. The developers addressed Team Arena, explaining it was temporarily removed due to tedium and gear-swapping friction, with a reworked version planned for later in the year. They also discussed player feedback regarding the endgame seasonal boss Phase 2, noting they are re-evaluating pacing and progression balance. Furthermore, the team explained that early-season stamina and event limitations are intentional design choices to encourage strategic resource management. Finally, the developers acknowledged that exchange shops lose value over time and confirmed they are exploring shop refreshes and long-term resource sinks.
meta_changes: Team Arena rework is planned for late year to streamline mechanics, reduce gear swapping, and reduce time commitment across seasons.
Endgame seasonal boss Phase 2 pacing and mechanics are being re-evaluated based on player feedback to reduce tedium.
Alliance, Journey, and Glory exchange shops are being evaluated for future refreshes or meaningful late-season resource sinks.
tips: Plan early-season stamina and resource spending strictly, as developers intentionally limit early resources to prioritize strategic account progression over farming.
Expect stamina rewards to expand significantly toward the end of each season to serve as a catch-up mechanic.

videos.summary: This video breaks down the Sep 1 patch changes to the Temporal Vortex Cloudtop Arbor (Arbor Hydra Noctuaa / Diurna) boss fight. The update added a blocked tile to prevent manual egg manipulation and reduced the number of eggs spawned during the boss's weakened phase from 4 to 3. This resulted in a massive damage nerf to AoE-focused teams, especially Toxin (Serpentemis) teams whose damage fell by nearly 50%. Skratch tests optimal board positioning to salvage Toxin DPS and covers strategy tips for the Bloom & Bounty event.

heroes.name: Serpentemis
heroes.verdict: Heavy AoE damage loss in Vortex
heroes.note: Takes a massive damage hit in Temporal Vortex Noctuaa because fewer eggs spawn during vulnerable boss phases and egg placement cannot be grouped as tightly.

heroes.name: Reytah
heroes.note: Requires precise grid positioning to handle egg knockbacks and maintain optimal AoE target coverage.

teams.note: Toxin team DPS dropped from 13.8B down to ~7.6B-8.5B following the egg spawn count and grid layout patch.

meta_changes: Temporal Vortex Noctuaa blocked a key grid tile next to the boss head, disabling the strategy of forcing eggs to spawn tightly grouped together.
Arbor Hydra Noctuaa now spawns 3 eggs instead of 4 while under vulnerable penalty states, significantly reducing total AoE damage output for all teams.
tips: In the Bloom & Bounty event, allow Exotic Blooms to complete their entire 10-hour growth cycle to reach maturity before harvesting to maximize Mythic gear drop rates.
Reposition heroes in a straight grid line in Temporal Vortex Noctuaa to maximize AoE damage coverage across the newly spaced-out egg spawns.

videos.summary: OddOneGaming showcases three high-performing teams for the Crown Contest Lightning Guardian boss, achieving over 7 billion total damage across three rounds. The guide highlights an Aura team doing ~3.2B damage, a Toxin team doing ~1.9B damage, and a Corrosion team doing ~2.1B damage. Detailed equipment sets, hero stat priorities, and artifact synergies are explained for each composition. Key mechanics include using healers with Gatekeeper's Staff to turn overhealing into shields and teamwide damage buffs, as well as optimizing attack order and stat thresholds for maximum ultimate energy gains.

heroes.name: Talethia
heroes.note: Requires the highest Attack and Crit Damage in the team so Shahla and Lincos target her with their ultimate energy and stat buffs.

heroes.name: Shahla
heroes.note: Uses the Destiny's Will talent to continuously grant ultimate energy and Aura energy to Talethia when her ultimate bounces.

heroes.name: Diantha
heroes.note: Equipped with Witch's Remains artifact to consistently inflict defense penalties on the boss targets.

heroes.name: Lincos
heroes.note: Wears Puppeteer's Inspiration set to speed up ultimate rotation for same-element allies, with recast timing set to 15s if needed.

heroes.name: Anneliesis
heroes.note: Provides healing and team damage buffs using Moonlight's Grace and Devout Prayer sets; can be substituted with Solmo, Acilia, or Rena.

heroes.name: Oggok
heroes.note: Equipped with Gatekeeper's Staff, Moonlight's Grace, and Devout Prayer to convert overhealing into team shields and damage buffs.

heroes.name: Sleight
heroes.note: Wears Puppeteer's Inspiration and Golden Antlers; can be replaced by other poison appliers like Corrin.

heroes.name: Serpentemis
heroes.note: Built full damage with Statue of the Serpent Deity artifact to maximize poison derivative damage.

heroes.name: Twitch
heroes.note: Wears Ilhuya's Fang, Whirling Edge, and Bardic Inspiration weapon to maximize poison debuff landing and damage output.

heroes.name: Durango
heroes.note: Uses Misty Conch and Bardic Inspiration weapon to help maintain debuff uptime while providing team utility.

heroes.name: Sacredeia
heroes.note: Built with Golden Alarm artifact and near 100% Crit Rate for strong AoE damage output.

heroes.name: Whisk
heroes.note: Built full damage with Swamp Toadstool artifact to maximize Corrosion derivative damage.

heroes.name: Calavera
heroes.note: Uses Gatekeeper's Staff to convert overhealing into shields, triggering Secrecy Order's Chant and Devout Prayer team buffs.

heroes.name: Rook
heroes.note: Built with 100% Crit Rate and Puppeteer's Inspiration to supply extra ultimate energy to Corrosion allies.

heroes.name: Reytah
heroes.note: Equipped with Misty Conch, Sacred River's Revelation, and Moonlight's Grace to provide healing and damage amplification.

teams.note: Achieves ~3.2B damage; relies on Shahla feeding ultimate energy to Talethia while Lincos wears Puppeteer's Inspiration.
Achieves ~1.9B damage; relies on Oggok overheal shielding to maintain team buffs while Serpentemis and Twitch deal massive Toxin damage.
Achieves ~2.13B damage; high-investment Corrosion composition using Calavera's overhealing to trigger shield-activated team damage buffs.

tips: Ensure your main Aura DPS (Talethia) has the highest Attack stat on the team so single-target Attack-based buffs land on her instead of supports.
Equip high-volume healers like Oggok and Calavera with Gatekeeper's Staff alongside Devout Prayer or Secrecy Order's Chant to turn overhealing into shields that grant teamwide damage buffs.
Include at least one hero wearing the Puppeteer's Inspiration set in elemental teams to feed ultimate energy to same-element allies.
Golden Tresym is the preferred familiar for multi-target boss encounters to increase AoE damage taken by enemies.
If missing specific Toxin or Corrosion legendaries, substitute with your best AoE damage compositions in Burn (Durem), Thunderbolt, Rally, or Dauntless.

videos.summary: This guide covers the Psychicore Elemental Affinity tree progression and optimal Affinity Solvent allocation. At Tier III, players should prioritize Attack and HP nodes for their primary team element, while taking only Attack nodes for secondary teams. Tier IV prioritizes Accuracy over Resistance for landing debuffs in PvE and PvP. Tier V and VI focus on maxing Elemental Damage Bonus before moving to defensive stats, leading up to powerful tier VII offensive boosts.
meta_changes: Elemental Affinity unlocks on Day 3 of a new server.
Higher tiers of Elemental Affinity require deploying 5 heroes of the corresponding elemental group to gain maximum affinity bonuses, compared to 3 heroes in earlier tiers.
tips: At Tier III, fully invest in both Attack % and HP % for your main elemental team, but only invest in Attack % for your secondary and tertiary teams.
Prioritize Accuracy over Resistance at Tier IV to land debuffs and control effects consistently.
Max out Elemental Damage Bonus at Tier V (10 points) to unlock Tier VI.
Prioritize offensive nodes over defensive nodes in higher tiers to maximize overall team damage output.
Farm Affinity Solvent diligently from Fey Meander, Temporal Vortex, Alliance Gameplay, Arena, Continental Challenge, and Otherworld Exploration to keep your account power competitive.
videos.title: Psychicore Guide - Where to Spend Affinity Solvent | Beginner Series | Dragonheir x Dragonstride

videos.summary: This video breaks down Continental Challenge boss Talethia and evaluates the viability of Thunderbolt teams against her. Talethia's stage mechanics heavily incentivize Enlightenment damage instances and running a three-element team for a 50% damage bonus, excluding damage over time like Toxin. Skratch tests four different Thunderbolt team variations featuring new hero Tariz alongside Perkunte and Alaura, experimenting with different support combinations. The boss deals extreme burst damage that makes surviving the full duration nearly impossible without exclusive supports and favorable RNG on survival skills like Rena's unkillable buff. Due to extreme difficulty and survivability issues, Skratch recommends holding Thunderbolt teams for the final week of the challenge rather than using them early.

heroes.verdict: Solid Thunderbolt DPS/debuffer, but not an urgent summon
heroes.note: Inflicts Gaze via his battle skill to reduce enemy attack speed and recharge speed by 30%, but the skill's timing can make consistent boss cycle alignment tricky.

heroes.name: Perkunte
heroes.note: Rapidly stacks the stage Enlightenment attack bonus through his multi-hit skills, but is extremely vulnerable to being one-shot by Talethia's AoE.

heroes.name: Alaura
heroes.note: Best equipped with her exclusive artifact Flowering Lyre or Punisher's Whip to support team derivative damage and apply recharge speed penalties.

heroes.name: Rena
heroes.note: Provides crucial shields, healing, and battle skill unkillable buffs that are mandatory to survive Talethia's burst phases.

heroes.name: Journ
heroes.note: Casts ultimates rapidly without manual timing, dispels boss buffs, drains ultimate energy, and enables the three-element 50% damage boost.

heroes.name: Scaarr
heroes.note: Equipped with Punisher's Whip, he provides reliable damage reduction, team damage amplification, and recharge speed penalties, enabling the highest score of 693M.

heroes.name: Solmo
heroes.note: Even when built with high defense and Aurelum Vest, he lacks the raw mitigation required to survive Talethia's scaling damage.

heroes.name: Torrin
heroes.verdict: Weak budget healer for this boss
heroes.note: Tested with Everlasting Diamond and Gatekeeper's Staff, but his shields and healing output fall far short of keeping the team alive.

teams.note: Three-element setup triggering the 50% stage damage bonus; scored between 568M and 682M damage on default skill timings, but wiped before the 5-minute mark.
Top scoring composition reaching 693M damage; Scaarr uses Punisher's Whip to delay boss ultimates while buffing team mitigation and damage.
Non-exclusive support test that survived under 3 minutes and scored only 354M to 357M due to inadequate survivability.
Full elemental affinity setup utilizing multiple exclusive supports; survived the full 5 minutes but lacked sufficient damage output, scoring 573M.

meta_changes: Continental Challenge boss difficulty has scaled significantly compared to earlier seasons, demanding multiple exclusive supports at Inspiration 1+ to endure enrage mechanics.
Stage property awards 1% ATK per instance of Enlightenment damage (up to 40 stacks, excluding DoTs) and grants a 50% damage boost if three distinct elements are deployed.
tips: Do not use Toxin against Talethia because damage over time does not trigger the stage Enlightenment attack buff stacks.
Avoid Wild teams on Talethia because the archetype requires four DPS slots, leaving insufficient room for the two or three defensive supports needed to survive.
Equip Punisher's Whip on frequent ultimate casters like Scaarr to trigger Recharge Speed Penalty and slow down Talethia's ultimate cycle.
Run skills on default timings instead of manually tuning skill rotations, as Tariz's recharge debuffs cause complex timers to desync.
Hold Thunderbolt attempts until the final week of Continental Challenge to see if meta strategies improve or boss tuning changes.

While heavily invested Aura teams hit a wall due to these immunities, Shadow teams excel because they output tremendous raw critical damage without needing debuffs. Saverio serves as the primary damage carry, while heroes with ultimate energy manipulation (such as Ripekas or Fathomdown) help survive deadly enemy ultimates.

heroes.name: Ripekas
heroes.note: Can replace Berengar for Stage 120 due to ultimate energy manipulation, delaying devastating enemy ultimate skills.

heroes.name: Torrin
heroes.note: Provides stealth and bonus stats to the team, allowing damage dealers to survive initial bursts.

heroes.name: Fathomdown
heroes.note: A strong tank alternative capable of manipulating enemy ultimate energy when control debuffs are blocked.

heroes.name: Anneliesis
heroes.note: Her debuff-reliant kit and control become useless for the first 60 seconds due to undispellable enemy immunity.

videos.summary: Skratch ranks all 12 damage schools in Dragonheir: Silent Gods based on their overall account impact, progression power, PvP viability, and endgame boss performance. Aura and Dauntless take top spots alongside Ice Blast and Toxin, while Thunderbolt and Frost land at the bottom.
